item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: I liked this a lot, and I identified it as SCP-507-inspired on first reading, even though I was aware it wasn't quite the same model.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: You know, it probably would be better under that position. The use of SCP-507 was primarily inspirational, rather than a translation from SCP. If I felt the urge to re-write it, I would probably switch it over to a normal D-class, though my own irregular work ethic will unfortunately decide that. That's not to excuse myself for not rewriting it, which I should and may, but it is to say that there isn't an especially good chance of it occurring, from my perspective.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: The way you have it written is very structured on purpose, I believe. So if it's not in this formatting, it'd probably be hard to convey it otherwise. I don't think that's an issue you can fix (as far as I know), but if you do fix it, I'd be glad to look at it again. I also agree with Gaffney above.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: I liked it stylistically (the key aspect here is the repetition of story and structure with gradual changes each time) and content-wise, but I found the story impossible to connect to SCP-507. I thought it followed the degradation of a man's life until he ended up as a D-Class.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
I can say that I liked this, a lot. I really didn't realize which skip was until I read the comments, but learning who the character was just made it better (because I understood what was going on).

I don't know, but the style is so minimalistic it freaked me out, like when one is playing those weird horror indie games or reading Phillip K. Dick. May be I just like stories that leave me confused until the end.

Either way, 'nuff rambling. Take my +1

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
It's about 507! I almost thought it was about a D-class transiting from normal life to life under the Foundation. It's quite vague as it is, if that's the case. That said, I do like the nonchalant "It's normal" tone of the article.

In any case, I will invoke Death of the Author (as in, I will disregard authorial intent and interpret the article in my own way) here and upvote it on that basis.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
While there is a lot of room for thematic, stylistic, and even conceptual tinkering when writing something based off of something else here, there usually needs to be something to justify it. This doesn't really have it, and so by the end, I was just confused about why he suddenly had a wife in one dimension, why he has a job, etc.

There's potential here, but I think it needs some reworking.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded: Understandable. Do you think that there could be some way to fix or correct that, or is it at the actual core writing of the thing? Is there any potential way that that could be alleviated?
